title: Fuel Efficiency & Calorific Value
description: How do scientists measure which fuel gives the most energy? Master calorific value to power the Guardian Flame.

content.value: How do we compare fuels fairly? We use the CALORIFIC VALUE — the amount of heat energy produced when 1 kilogram of a fuel is completely burnt. A higher calorific value means the fuel gives more energy per kilogram.
Calorific value is measured in kilojoules per kilogram (kJ/kg). The bigger the number, the more heat you get from each kilogram of fuel — so it's a more efficient fuel.

CALORIFIC VALUE (approx, kJ/kg) — higher = more energy
Cow dung cake   ~  6,000–8,000
Wood            ~ 17,000
Coal            ~ 25,000–33,000
Petrol          ~ 45,000
LPG             ~ 55,000
Hydrogen        ~ 150,000  (the highest!)

Hydrogen has the highest calorific value of all fuels, and it burns to form only water — no pollution! This makes it a very promising clean fuel for the future, though it is still tricky and expensive to store and handle safely.
Higher calorific value = more heat per kilogram = a more efficient fuel. LPG beats wood, and hydrogen beats everything — plus hydrogen is clean.

Key Takeaway: Calorific value is the heat produced by completely burning 1 kg of a fuel, measured in kJ/kg. A higher calorific value means a more efficient fuel. Hydrogen has the highest calorific value and burns cleanly.
